kind: workload specification, not an executable load generator

perInstance.runtime: one Archipel process, one independent database, one real Prosody service

primarySharedTopology.nativeAccess: direct native c2s login at home; local MUC or authenticated s2s to the authoritative room host
primarySharedTopology.webAccess: normal home channel when hosting the room; explicit channel bridge to its authoritative XMPP room otherwise
primarySharedTopology.projectionRateAssumption: local room commits and bridged foreign message copies each append xmpp_events; relay echoes of already saved local posts are suppressed
primarySharedTopology.occupancyAssumption: one resource/room per native user; bridge owners are benchmark web members, with no extra administrative listener accounts

phases.name: cold-start
phases.purpose: measure authentication, channel bootstrap, MAM and presence separately
phases.readiness: all SSE streams open, all native clients bound and room-joined, initial web history and native archive loads completed

phases.name: local-steady-state
phases.role: comparison baseline; primary workload is the shared-room phase

phases.name: shared-rooms-all-five-instances
phases.foreignRoomRouting: each of the 100 authoritative rooms contains 15 web and 5 native users from every instance
phases.writes: each user writes in their assigned shared room, one total message per user per minute
phases.transport: real certificate-authenticated Prosody s2s, native c2s, MUC and explicit Archipel channel bridges

phases.name: denser-shared-rooms
phases.role: follow-up fan-out stress phase after the primary workload

phases.name: optional-fwdxp
phases.purpose: measure signed FWDXP channel replication separately from XMPP s2s
phases.foreignChannelRouting: spread evenly over 20 channels and four peers
phases.requirements: real signed subscriptions and deliveries, default pacing baseline and an explicitly labelled tuned pacing run

metrics: offered, admitted, dropped, committed and failed writes by transport and instance
unique senders, native joins/disconnects, MAM latency, room membership and presence stability
message commit-to-first-visible latency using stable IDs; missing and duplicate live deliveries
bootstrap completion; refresh admission delay separately from request service latency
native sync payload bytes, duration, HTTP errors, cursor lag and event backlog
bridge virtual-resource count, remote-room sync duration, receive callbacks and duplicate per-resource processing
projection event production including bridge copies versus native sync drain rate; silent bridge-heartbeat updates versus user-visible notices
federation queued deliveries, distinct peer hosts, retries, duplicate delivery attempts and queue age
CPU, RSS, event-loop delay and database operations per instance plus generator lag
constraints: never count a socket write as successful room delivery
a phase without completed initial bootstrap is not steady state
keep native XMPP, browser-XMPP virtual occupants and FWDXP subscriptions distinct
all five origins must receive the same shared-room conversation through explicit supported bridges, not presumed FWDXP/XMPP forwarding
report every instance separately; cluster averages cannot hide a failed room host
preserve admission, blocking, revocation, room privacy and per-viewer filtering
use fresh data, private test credentials and an isolated network; do not use production instances
